title: Heavy-fermion hybridization waves from Dirac spinons near a Kondo-breakdown quantum phase transition
authors: Pedro M. Cônsoli, Matthias Vojta, Onur Erten
abstract: Motivated by the recent observation of spatially modulated screening in different paramagnetic heavy-fermion materials, we propose a theoretical mechanism for the emergence of such hybridization waves in frustrated Kondo lattices with no magnetic order. By applying a parton mean-field theory and a perturbative calculation to a minimal Kondo-Heisenberg lattice model, we demonstrate that a heavy Fermi liquid can naturally develop hybridization waves when it approaches a quantum phase transition where Kondo screening breaks down and the local magnetic moments form a Dirac spin liquid. We relate the strength of this mechanism to a kinematic condition on the electronic and spinon band structures and show that the spatial periodicity of the hybridization wave is set by a momentum $\vec{Q}$ connecting the nodes in the dispersion of the Dirac spinons to low-energy portions of the electronic band structure.
summary: This theoretical work investigates how hybridization waves can emerge in heavy-fermion materials near a quantum phase transition where Kondo screening breaks down. Using mean-field theory on a Kondo-Heisenberg lattice, the authors predict that the wave's periodicity is determined by the geometry connecting Dirac spinon nodes to the conduction electron band structure. It provides a detailed theoretical framework for understanding modulated electronic states in strongly correlated quantum magnets.
main_problem: The paper proposes a theoretical mechanism for the emergence of spatially modulated hybridization waves (HWs) in frustrated Kondo lattices that remain paramagnetic and exhibit no magnetic order.
main_result: HWs are predicted to arise when a heavy Fermi liquid approaches a Kondo-breakdown quantum phase transition into a state featuring a Dirac spin liquid (DSL). The wave's periodicity is set by a momentum connecting nodes in the Dirac spinon dispersion to the electronic band structure.
method: The analysis employs a combination of parton mean-field theory, Hubbard-Stratonovich transformations, and perturbative calculations applied to a minimal Kondo-Heisenberg lattice model.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by a Kondo-Heisenberg lattice Hamiltonian coupling conduction electrons ($H_t$) to local moments ($H_K, H_H$). The study analyzes the competition between Kondo screening and inter-moment interactions.
key_observables: Kondo screening strength ($|b_a|$), bond variables ($\chi_{jb,ia}$), and four fluxes ($\Phi_1, \dots, \Phi_4$) characterizing the spinon state.
important_parameters: Kondo temperature ($T_K$), intermoment exchange ($J_H$), and the coupling strength $J_K$, which dictate the proximity to the Kondo-breakdown transition.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on large-N mean-field theory approximations, and some calculations assume invariance under two-site unit cell translations or restrict variables (e.g., real $\chi$ for DSL).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Kondo HW state relative to the heavy Fermi liquid phase in a phase diagram, and show the lattice structure and mean-field results for various variational states (VBS, CSL, DSL) as a function of coupling parameters.
paper_structure: The paper develops the mean-field theory for the Kondo-Heisenberg model, analyzes the pure f-sector variational states (VBS, CSL, DSL) by minimizing the free energy, and finally connects the emergence of HWs to the intersection of the $c$-electron Fermi surface with the Dirac spinon nodes near the quantum critical point.
why_interesting: The detailed theoretical mapping of a quantum phase transition in a strongly correlated system, linking itinerant electron behavior (Fermi liquid) to localized moment physics (spin liquid) via a modulated state, is highly relevant to understanding exotic quantum materials.

figures.caption: Figure 1. (a) Kondo hybridization wave (HW) with a two- sublattice unit cell and ordering wavevector Q on the triangu- lar lattice. The spatial profile of Kondo screening is encoded in the radii of the spheres surrounding the local magnetic moments. Blue and red spheres mark the different sublat- tices. (b) Schematic zero-temperature phase diagram of a Kondo lattice as a function of the Kondo coupling JK. The HW emerges at intermediate couplings, between a fractional- ized Fermi liquid with a Dirac spin-liquid component (FL∗ DSL) and a uniformly-screened heavy Fermi liquid. The yellow star marks the Kondo-breakdown (KB) transition.

Figure 2. (a) Triangular lattice with sublattices A and B. The unit cell of our mean-field calculations is illustrated in the center, where we have labeled the four independent fluxes, Φ1, . . . , Φ4, and represented the six χ fields as directed bonds of different colors. (b) Mean-field phase diagram for L = 150, JH = 0.2, κ = 1, and kBT = 10−3. The hatched portions correspond to hybridization waves (HW), which arise in the proximity of a fractionalized Fermi liquid (FL∗ 0π0π). The dashed lines separate regions with spatially uniform (right) and nematic (left) absolute values of the χ fields. Different flux sectors are distinguished by the colors in the background.
